payload.summary: Ran the /iterate-on-implementation refinement pass over Phase 3's diff (needs_user.py, the three lifecycle hooks, and their tests) and found one real bug in the Step 11.5 partial-pair (F6) cleanup: `git checkout -- $JSON_PATH $MD_PATH` was followed unconditionally by `rm -f $JSON_PATH $MD_PATH`, so whenever a prior audit had already committed the ledger pair and a later run truncated one file mid-write, the checkout correctly restored the tracked file to its committed content and the very next line deleted it again — leaving a clean, previously-committed pair showing as deleted in `git status`. Fixed it to branch per path on `git ls-files --error-unmatch` exactly as design.md's F6 prose specifies, and added an executable test (not just a content pin) that extracts the real cleanup snippet from the SKILL.md fence and runs it against real git repos for both shapes; verified it fails against the old logic and passes against the fix. All four required gates pass; branch pushed.

decisions.title: Branch the F6 orphan-cleanup per path on `git ls-files --error-unmatch`, not unconditionally on both paths
decisions.rationale: design.md's F6 section explicitly names `git ls-files --error-unmatch` as the per-path discriminator: a path it knows is restored with `git checkout --`, a path it does not know (the first-audit case) is removed with `rm -f`. The implementation instead ran both commands unconditionally on both paths every time, which only produces the right result when both paths happen to be untracked (the common first-audit case) — but silently deletes a tracked, just-restored file whenever a later audit truncates one half of an already-committed pair (e.g. choices.json corrupted/emptied mid-write while choices.md still holds its prior committed content). Fixed to match the design's explicit per-path loop.

decisions.title: Add an executable test alongside the content pins for the F6 cleanup, rather than only strengthening the string-match test
decisions.rationale: The existing test_orphan_cleanup_names_tracked_and_untracked_cases only asserted the strings 'git checkout --' and 'rm -f' appear somewhere in the section — it could not have caught the unconditional-sequential-commands bug, since both strings are present either way. Per the repo's TDD/prove-it convention, added a test that extracts the literal cleanup snippet from the SKILL.md fence and executes it in real temp git repos for both reachable partial-pair shapes, so a future edit that reintroduces the same class of bug fails a real assertion instead of a string search.

next_steps: No further iteration needed on my read of this diff against design.md F1-F8; hand off to the next autopilot phase (vendor review / validate-feature) per the orchestrator's normal sequence

If a future iteration touches Step 11.5 again, re-run skills/tests/audit-choices/test_workflow_hooks.py::TestIterateOnImplementationStep11_5::test_orphan_cleanup_behavior specifically — it is the only test that actually executes the cleanup logic rather than pattern-matching prose
